record.context_brief: Hyperbolic manifolds: p-isospectral but not strongly isospectral
record.original_question: Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds that are p-isospectral for every degree p, meaning the Hodge-Laplace operators on p-forms all have the same spectra, but are nevertheless not strongly isospectral?

evidence.quote: Question 8.11. Are there hyperbolic manifolds p-isospectral for all p that are not strongly isospectral?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. For each integer $p$ with $0\le p\le \dim M$, let $\Delta_p$ denote the Hodge–Laplace operator acting on smooth $p$-forms on $M$, and let $\mathrm{Spec}_p(M)$ denote its spectrum (counted with multiplicities). Two closed Riemannian manifolds $M_1, M_2$ are said to be $p$-isospectral if $\mathrm{Spec}_p(M_1)=\mathrm{Spec}_p(M_2)$, and they are said to be strongly isospectral if, for every natural elliptic differential operator $D$ canonically associated to the Riemannian structure (equivalently, for every locally invariant elliptic operator built from the metric, including all twisted Laplacians on sections of natural bundles), the spectra of $D$ on $M_1$ and on $M_2$ coincide.

A hyperbolic manifold is a complete Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$.

Question: Do there exist closed hyperbolic manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$ that are $p$-isospectral for every $p\in\{0,1,\dots,\dim M_1\}$ but are not strongly isospectral?
artifact.status_search_result: A direct search did not surface any construction of hyperbolic manifolds that are $p$-isospectral for all $p$ yet fail to be strongly isospectral. Known examples of isospectral hyperbolic manifolds (e.g., via Sunada's method) tend to yield strong isospectrality, and recent work has produced strongly isospectral hyperbolic 3-manifolds distinguished by finer invariants (such as cohomology ring structure), but the converse separation—$p$-isospectral for all $p$ without strong isospectrality—does not appear to be resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Strongly isospectral hyperbolic 3-manifolds with nonisomorphic rational cohomology rings
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of strongly isospectral hyperbolic 3-manifolds distinguished by cohomology ring structure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on strongly isospectral hyperbolic manifolds, not on the separation between all-p-isospectrality and strong isospectrality.

status_evidence.title: Constructing multi-cusped hyperbolic manifolds that are isospectral and not isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of isospectral non-isometric hyperbolic manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Standard constructions produce isospectral pairs typically obtained via Sunada-type methods, which yield strong isospectrality.
